subject: DPA: GDPR transfer impact and SCCs for Acme Health
content:
From: Jordan Mills <legal@acmehealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: Redwood DPA redlines + SCCs – follow up

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call earlier. We've attached our consolidated redlines to the DPA and a tracker for the SCCs. High-level items we need clarity on:

- Transfer Impact Addendum (TIA): we flagged a few subprocessors and would like confirmation Redwood can provide EU-to-US transfer controls (logs, encryption at rest, key control).
- SCCs: we proposed a narrow set of processor to processor obligations; please confirm Redwood's acceptance or proposed language.
- Roles and data mapping: we included a table showing where Acme PHI/PII flows into your runtime and asked for a statement on who is controller/processor for telemetry and logs.

Attachment stubs: Acme_DPA_Redlines_v3.docx, SCCs_tracking_sheet.xlsx

Could you let me know expected timeline for legal review and whether your privacy team wants to jump on a short call?

Regards,
Jordan Mills
Senior Counsel, Acme Health
--

On Thu, 11 Sep 2025 at 09:03, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 11 Sep 2025 04:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + SCCs – follow up

Hi Jordan — thanks for the materials. We're reviewing internally. Quick notes up front:

- We can accept the SCCs in principle; there are a couple of clause edits (security testing notice period and subprocessors list) we propose to keep operationally workable.
- On TIA: we may need to provide additional evidence (KMS summary, region routing controls). I will confirm with infra today.
- Roles: Redwood is processor for customer data in inference APIs; telemetry (error rates, performance metrics) is described in our MSA as operational telemetry and is scoped as processor operations, but we can add clarifying language to the DPA.

Looping in Laura (Legal Ops) and Karthik (Product) to weigh in on the SCC edits and TIA evidence.

Next step: internal legal to produce a redline for your doc by EOD Monday 15 Sept. Would that timeline work?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

--

On Fri, 12 Sep 2025 at 11:20, laura_bennett@redwood.com wrote:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: FW: Redwood DPA redlines + SCCs – follow up

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Jordan's packet. I reviewed the tracker and proposed a short set of responses. Key internal asks for the review: 

1) Karthik — can you confirm whether telemetry logs include full request/response payloads for PII? We need to determine if telemetry should be carved out or subject to stronger access controls.
2) Vivek — please pull a short blurb on our KMS practices and whether customer-managed keys are available for Acme (they are not today, but we have envelope encryption options).
3) Kimberly — I'll draft the inline redline to Jordan's DPA and propose alternate SCC language for the security testing clause.

I suggest we keep the first reply to Acme high-level (accept SCCs in principle + request time to push back on 2-3 operational items). If they ask for a TIA, we can provide the standard export controls and a TIA template.

Laura
Legal Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--

On Mon, 15 Sep 2025 at 09:05, karthik_iyer@redwood.com wrote:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + SCCs – follow up

Laura / Kimberly — quick answers from product infra:

- Telemetry: we log high-level request metadata (model id, token counts, latencies, anonymized request identifiers). We do NOT persist full request/response payloads in telemetry by default. There are opt-in debug logs for enterprise customers that can include full payloads; these are only available behind an EVP and require DPA-level controls.
- Subprocessors: current list attached in our standard subprocessor notice (link in tracker). We will need to preserve a 30-day notice for new subprocessors.
- Customer-managed keys: not generally available in hosted plan; for Dedicated/Private deployments we do support bring-your-own-KMS.

If Acme needs full payload logging turned on, that requires a dedicated contract addendum and controls (audit trail, access request process).

Karthik
VP Product
Redwood Inference

--

On Tue, 16 Sep 2025 at 15:47, kimberly_park@redwood.com wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Mills <legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@acmehealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 11:47:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + SCCs – follow up

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Attached is Redwood's consolidated response (see inline redline and SCC tracker). Summary below: 

- SCCs: Accepted in principle. We proposed small edits: 1) security testing notification window changed to 5 business days (we included language that testing won't impact production), and 2) clarified subprocessors list and notification process (30 days notice + emergency subprocessor clause).
- TIA/Transfers: We can provide the standard TIA template and the following evidence: KMS summary (regions & key handling), export controls doc, and our subprocessors list. Customer-managed keys are supported on Dedicated/Private deployments; envelope encryption options exist for hosted.
- Telemetry & Roles: Clarified in DPA that Redwood is processor; telemetry is limited to anonymized operational metrics unless explicitly enabled via enterprise debug logging (which requires an addendum).

Next steps: 
- Jordan: please confirm whether Acme needs full debug logging or if the anonymized telemetry is sufficient for your compliance team.
- Acme procurement: if you require customer-managed keys or Dedicated deployment for key control, let us know and we can surface pricing and timeline.
- Laura/Karthik/Vivek: if there are no further internal questions, I'll send the formal redline and our SCCs response to Jordan and ask for an alignment call this week.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_Response_v1.docx (inline redline), SCCs_tracking_sheet.xlsx

Best regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
